neighbours.label: The indefinite place adverbs ' somewhere', ' anywhere', ' elsewhere', ' everywhere' (and weaker ' wherever'), in any context; peaks strongest on ' somewhere' and ' anywhere'
fire: If you are looking for a quiet place to read, you can probably find a free table somewhere in the library basement.
Our guide told us that you cannot get fresh mangoes like these anywhere else in the whole province.
Every winter my grandfather insists that his old fishing hat is lying somewhere in the garage, buried under boxes.
The experienced pilot said the storm could hit anywhere along the coast before dawn, so everyone should be prepared.
Scientists believe that a planet with liquid water may exist somewhere in the habitable zone of that distant star.
She searched the whole apartment for her keys but they were not anywhere that she could see.
After the move, we realized we needed somewhere to store the bicycles and the old winter coats.
The charity noticed that hunger shows up everywhere in the region, not just in the largest cities.
quiet: Readers who want a calm spot will find plenty of free tables near the windows of the library basement.
Fresh mangoes like these grow only in the sunny southern valleys of the province, according to our guide.
My grandfather insists that his old fishing hat is lying in the garage, buried under a pile of boxes.
Everyone should be prepared, the weathered pilot warned, because the storm will hit the coast before dawn.
A planet with liquid water may well orbit in the habitable zone of that distant star, scientists believe.
Her keys were nowhere to be seen after she searched the whole apartment from top to bottom.
We realized after the move that a shed was needed to store the bicycles and the old winter coats.
Hunger is common in the region, the charity noticed, and not just in the largest cities nearby.

notes: Label and sentences written blind by a Claude subagent from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt.md, identical for Haiku, Sonnet and Opus); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus comparison on the same 48 poles.
